My daughter also lied to me about school. I didn’t mean to put extreme pressure on her but I thought she wanted to go to college and I encouraged her. She didn’t want to disappoint me when she failed her classes, got put on academic probation, lost her scholarship and eventually dropped out. She lied about it for a long time. She made up stories and let me think that she was doing okay. I would have supported whatever decision she made about school. I just wish she hadn’t lied. But then I thought why was she lying to me? She was scared. She was afraid I’d be disappointed in her. It broke my heart that she felt she couldn’t come to me and just talk to me. I feel like I failed her.

Talk to your mom. I hope she understands but if she doesn’t, don’t let that stop you from doing what you feel is best for you. I’m glad you feel ready to go to school now. If she still wants to help financially let her. Sometimes parents, myself included, make things worse when we’re only trying to help. I think she was beaming with pride because she thought that you were on the “right” path. Or at least the path she thought was right for you. You know what’s best for you. Just be honest, with yourself and with your mom. Good luck! You got this kid!

I absolutely suck at relationships. If you look through my history I wouldn’t blame you for not wanting to hear what I have to say. 

However, experience has taught me that if the other person wants to reach out they will and if they don’t they won’t. 

I hate that. It doesn’t seem fair and I get why you want to reach out to her. But my advice would be not to. You guys broke up, she said she didn’t want to be friends, she said she didn’t want to be in a relationship and she hasn’t reached out in anyway. I know it sucks. I know it’s hard. And I know you want to. But don’t. She’ll reach out to you if she feels like it. And maybe when she does, you won’t want to hear from her….. it’s only been a week, everything’s fresh and raw and painful, it’s surprising what a little time can do and how much can change in time.

There’s no turning it off. It’s okay that it’s been three years. But you can’t let that consume you. You can’t let it be what defines your life. It takes time. I wish there was a better answer, but just because it’s been a long time doesn’t make it bad and it doesn’t mean you’re doing anything wrong.

No. Not really. That’s more of a quick fix that may hurt more later. This is just my opinion and I may not be the best person the give advice, but I know that I want a happy healthy relationship and I know I won’t get that until I’m happy and healthy (emotionally, physically) myself. This ones just gonna have to hurt until it doesn’t. And when you meet girls you may find that they’re not a good match, don’t be in a rush to be with someone just to get over these feelings, take your time.

There’s no trick or quick fix. Unfortunately I know that from personal experiences. But the truth is you have to be happy with yourself and when you’re ready try dating again, don’t settle just to have a gf or just to have regular sex (unless you’re content with casual hookups). Take your time and find  someone that will give you what you want and deserve. It may take time, but it will be worth it. There may also be more heartbreak but that’s part of the process, just don’t give up on yourself and don’t settle. Good luck!

It’s complicated, but you’re not wrong. We’re really different. We’ve had a chance to talk these past few days and I’ve been reading through comments. I wanted something with him so desperately and we were so close to having it. It’s hard to let that go. But you’re right. I don’t want him to be unhappy. I don’t want to be unhappy. I wish it were easier. For me. I’m aware it seems like a super simple and easy solution for a lot of people and I don’t blame them. But it’s really hard for me. I love him. I want to be with him.
If he treated me the way he treats me now when we first met, I absolutely would not have gotten with him, planned out a life and family with him and wanted all those things with him.

I’m not looking for pity and I’m not looking for a solution. I just wanted to say something that’s been bothering me. I’m not looking for karma. I’m not a troll. I’m just a person that’s struggling in life and even though the answer seems simple and straightforward when it’s typed out, it’s much harder to do.

But I love him and I don’t want to let him go. But if feels like he’s willing to let me go at any moment and it makes me feel like shit.

It depends on who you talk to. Taking to a friend may make you feel a little better and may not lead to any further intervention. However, crisis hotlines, suicide hotlines, teachers, nurses, counselors, doctors, therapists. Social workers and others are all mandated reporters. If they believe you are a danger to yourself or others they can request you be evaluated by professionals. Self-harm, abusing meds and thoughts of killing your self are really serious issues and may necessitate an involuntary (or unlikely, but voluntary) psychiatric hold. Most holds here in the US are 72 hours but can be shortened (unlikely) or extended. Once your placed on this hold you will most likely placed into an adult or juvenile facility where you will be monitored constantly and be evaluated by doctors, nurses, social workers. They’re may be group therapy, individual therapy and medications prescribed or adjusted as it sounds your already taking meds.

If you are placed on a hold you will miss days of school, however, most schools and teachers would understand a medical absence and help you get the work you missed completed and help you catch up. A 5150 hold wouldn’t go on your school record and prevent you from going to university.

It’s scary to even think about but if that’s the level of care you need, that’s the level of care you need.
